author: aditik06
title: feat: personalize the impulse-control cooldown by risk tolerance/literacy
decision: Replace single hardcoded COOLDOWN_MS for ImpulseControl.jsx with getCooldownMs(user) based on risk_tolerance and financial_literacy fields.
rationale: To personalize impulse-control cooldown by user's individual profile, which includes their willingness to take risks (risk_tolerance) as well as how comfortable they are managing finances without regret or impulsive decisions. This change provides a dynamic experience that adjusts according to the user's specific attributes rather than using an arbitrary fixed period for everyone.
alternatives: Keep single hardcoded COOLDOWN_MS
Implement different static cooldown periods based on risk_tolerance and financial_literacy values manually
source_excerpt:
feat: personalize the impulse-control cooldown by risk tolerance/literacy

ImpulseControl.jsx had a single hardcoded 48h COOLDOWN_MS for every
user. Replaced it with getCooldownMs(user), reading the risk_tolerance
and financial_literacy fields already collected at onboarding (via
useAuth()) and computing a duration from them.

Mapping (product judgment call, documented in code):
- Base hours by risk_tolerance: low=60, moderate=48, high=30 -
  anchored so risk_tolerance='moderate' lands exactly on the original
  fixed 48h, so the "average" profile's experience doesn't shift
  just because this landed; only the extremes move. A more
  risk-tolerant user needs less of a "wait it out" guardrail, a more
  risk-averse one keeps (or gets more of) it.
- Literacy nudges that base: beginner=+6h, intermediate=0,
  advanced=-6h - smaller than the risk-tolerance spread, since
  experience matters less than risk appetite for this guardrail.
- Floored at 24h regardless of combination (high+advanced, the
  shortest combo, lands exactly there) - even the most risk-tolerant,
  most experienced user still gets a full day to reconsider, not none.

Found and fixed a real bug while wiring this up: risk_tolerance's
actual values are 'low'/'moderate'/'high' (confirmed via
OnboardingPage.jsx and the live profile-edit form), not 'medium' as
models.py's stale inline comment claims - that column is an
unconstrained string, so nothing enforces the comment. Kept the
mapping keyed on the real runtime values instead.

Existing wishlist items aren't pinned to the old 48h - there's no
per-item cooldown duration persisted anywhere (and the issue scoped
this as frontend-only, reading fields that already exist), so every
item's remaining time is recomputed live from the CURRENT profile on
every render, same as new items. A later profile edit shifts the
remaining time on already-added items too - this is a deliberate
choice ("how long you wait" reflects who you are now), not an
oversight.

getTimeRemaining() and getElapsedPct() (the countdown ring, HH:MM:SS
display, and elapsed-percentage arc) now all read the per-render
cooldownMs instead of the old constant, and the card's subtitle
shows the actual computed hour count instead of a hardcoded "48".

Verified end-to-end in-browser: default (low + beginner) profile
showed "Wait 66 hours"; switching to high + advanced showed "Wait 24
hours"; moderate + advanced showed "Wait 42 hours" (confirms the
'moderate' key fix works, not just a lucky fallback); added a
wishlist item under the 42h profile and confirmed the countdown ring
started at 41:59, not 47:59.

Closes #47

author: aditik06
title: fix: guard against stranding a household when deleting an account
decision: Implementing the same ownership check as in leave_household for account deletion
rationale: To prevent stranding households when a sole owner deletes their own account. If there are other members, they must promote someone else before deleting.
alternatives: Continue allowing all users to delete accounts regardless of household membership status.
source_excerpt:
fix: guard against stranding a household when deleting an account

delete_account cleaned up the caller's HouseholdMember rows without
checking sole-ownership, unlike leave_household - a sole owner could
delete their account and strand the household with no owner.

Now mirrors leave_household's exact rule: if the caller is the only
owner of a household that still has other members, account deletion
is rejected (400, naming the household) until they promote someone
else first. If they're the sole owner AND the sole member, there's
nothing to strand, so that household is deleted outright as part of
the account deletion (same resolution leave_household uses for that
case) instead of being left as an empty, ownerless row.

Verified with a scripted scenario: blocked deletion while another
member remains (with the household correctly named in the error),
deletion succeeding after promoting another member to owner, and a
solo owner/solo member's account deletion cleanly removing both the
account and the now-fully-orphaned household.

author: aditik06
title: fix: revert shared transactions/goals to personal on household deletion
decision: Revert shared transactions/goals to personal instead of deleting them when a household is deleted.
rationale: A household disappearing shouldn't take anyone's logged financial data with it; each row's own user_id already tells you whose personal view it lands back in. This change ensures that after deletion, the related rows for households and members are removed while transactions/goals associated still appear correctly under an individual's account.
alternatives: Delete shared transactions/goals outright when a household is deleted.
source_excerpt:
fix: revert shared transactions/goals to personal on household deletion

_delete_household predates Transaction/Goal gaining a household_id
(that landed later in this same PR) and never got updated for it -
deleting a household left any transactions/goals tagged to it with a
dangling household_id, invisible to everyone (no one could pass the
now-nonexistent household in X-Household-Id, and they wouldn't show
in personal view either since household_id wasn't null).

Found this while merging in #51's delete_account fix, which calls
_delete_household from a new code path (account deletion) - without
this, that path would have started actively triggering the bug.

Now nulls household_id on both instead of deleting the rows outright
- a household disappearing shouldn't take anyone's logged financial
data with it, it just reverts to whoever's personal view it belongs
to via the row's own user_id.

Verified with a scripted scenario: a shared transaction and a shared
goal both survive household deletion with household_id reset to
null, correctly reappearing in the creator's personal view, while
the household itself and its members/invites are fully removed.

author: aditik06
title: feat: household tagging for transactions and goals
decision: _scope_filter function added to filter transactions based on active household ID
rationale: To ensure that users can only access their own untagged and tagged transactions for a specific household.
alternatives: Include all user's past linked housemates (if they had them)
Remove the filtering option entirely, leaving it up to front-end code
source_excerpt:
feat: household tagging for transactions and goals

PR 2 of 3 for #45 (household/shared accounts). Builds on PR 1's
Household/HouseholdMember models (#51) to make Transaction and Goal
optionally household-scoped - the only two tables the issue asks to
be shareable.

- Nullable household_id on Transaction and Goal; existing rows land
  as NULL (personal) with no behavior change for anyone not using
  households.
- New get_active_household_id dependency (auth.py): reads an
  optional X-Household-Id request header, validates the caller is
  actually a member, returns None otherwise. A header rather than a
  JWT claim, since the JWT isn't reissued on persona switch.
- Every transactions.py/goals.py query now scopes via a small
  _scope_filter helper: household_id == the active household, or
  (household_id IS NULL AND user_id == caller) when no header is
  sent - never a mix of personal and shared rows in one view.
- New GoalContribution model: every currentAmount change on PUT
  /goals/{id} is diffed against the pre-update value and recorded as
  a signed contribution (positive = deposit, negative = withdrawal)
  tagged to whoever made it, rather than only keeping a single
  running total. GoalResponse now includes the full contributions
  list for the frontend to render a per-member breakdown.
- household_id is always server-derived from the active-household
  header, never client-writable in the request body - same rule
  transactions.py already used for user_id.

Verified with a scripted end-to-end scenario: personal vs.
household-scoped transactions stay non-overlapping for the same
user, a second household member sees the shared transactions/goals,
a non-member is rejected (403) for a household they're not in, and
multi-user goal contributions (including a withdrawal as a negative
delta) are attributed to the correct user.

No frontend changes yet - that's PR 3.

Ref #45

alternatives: Leave the user alone but keep them listed (not preferred)
source_excerpt:
feat: household model, migration, invite + membership endpoints

PR 1 of 3 for #45 (household/shared accounts). Adds the Household /
HouseholdMember / HouseholdInvite models and migration, plus a
households router covering create, list, invite generation, join,
member listing, role promotion, member removal, leave, and explicit
deletion.

- Invites are short-lived 8-char codes (7-day expiry), not email -
  there is no mail infrastructure anywhere in this backend, and a
  code is the same zero-infra pattern Discord/Notion invites use.
- Multiple owners are allowed per household, so "the last owner"
  guard (leave/remove) just means "the only remaining owner" -
  promoting another member to owner is how you hand off before
  stepping down. A sole owner who is also the household's only
  remaining member can still leave; that's treated as equivalent to
  explicitly deleting the household rather than leaving it orphaned.
- DELETE /me now also cleans up the caller's HouseholdMember rows,
  extending the existing (pre-existing, not fully complete) cascade
  in that endpoint.

No transactions/goals are household-aware yet - that's PR 2. This PR
introduces no behavior change for any existing single-user flow.

Ref #45

author: aditik06
title: perf: stop paying the Ollama-unavailable tax on every AI call
decision: _ollama_unavailable_until set to _ollama_ready() return value. Introduced OLLAMA_RECHECK_SECONDS.
rationale: This change was introduced because Ollama's connection attempt, even after being refused by the OS/network-stack-level handling of a request.post(), takes several seconds (~4.1s). This time is paid for every call made to classify_transaction, generate_spending_alert, AND generate_financial_tips when OLLAMA is enabled but nothing else (the default) running on OLLAMA_HOST.
alternatives: _ollama_unavailable_until set to a fixed retry interval instead of using _ollama_ready().
source_excerpt:
perf: stop paying the Ollama-unavailable tax on every AI call

Profiled the actual bottleneck instead of guessing (per the issue's
suggested approach): with OLLAMA_ENABLED on (the default) but no
local Ollama daemon running, requests.post() to it doesn't fail fast
- it takes ~4.1s to be refused on this platform, confirmed with a
raw socket connect too (~2s, ruling out requests/urllib3 as the
cause - this is OS/network-stack-level connection-refusal handling,
which requests' own `timeout` parameter never gets a chance to
shortcut since the connection *is* refused, not silently dropped).
That's dead time paid on classify_transaction, generate_spending_alert,
AND generate_financial_tips - every single one, every single call.

Once a probe to Ollama fails, skip it entirely for 5 minutes instead
of re-attempting (and re-paying the ~4s tax) on the very next call.
A successful call resets the window immediately, so this only
affects the "Ollama enabled but not actually running" case - users
who do have it configured see no change.

Also adds timing logs around both the Ollama and Gemini paths on all
three call sites, so the actual latency split is visible going
forward instead of needing to re-profile blind next time.

Checked the other two hypotheses from the issue:
- NaturalLanguageInput.jsx already has a proper loading state
  (spinner, disabled input) - not the bottleneck, no change needed.
- Prompt-trimming / lighter local model for Quick Add's long prompt
  is left as a follow-up, not implemented here - no live Gemini/Ollama
  credentials available to validate an output-quality tradeoff, and
  the fix above is already a confirmed, measured win on its own.

Verified: a scripted before/after comparison shows the first Ollama
attempt still pays ~4.1s (unavoidable - that's the actual probe), but
every attempt afterward returns in <1ms for the next 5 minutes
instead of repeating the full delay.

Closes #12

author: aditik06
title: feat: add update_recurring action so "change X to Y" updates, not creates
decision: Added 'update_recurring' action to handle updates for existing plans instead of creating new ones.
rationale: The model's current behavior was incorrectly emitting create actions when users intended to update an existing plan, leading to unnecessary duplication. The decision ensures that only the changed fields are merged into a pre-existing RecurringPlan shape without duplicating it.
alternatives: Continue with 'recurring' action as is (incorrectly creating new plans instead of updating)
Implement additional checks before emitting create actions for recurring items
source_excerpt:
feat: add update_recurring action so "change X to Y" updates, not creates

"Change Google AI Pro subscription value to 650" was creating a brand
new "Google AI Pro Subscription" plan instead of updating the amount
on the existing "Google AI Pro" one - the prompt only had three action
shapes (transaction/debt/recurring), and an update-phrased request is
the closest fit to "recurring", so the model reasonably (but wrongly)
emitted a create action for it.

- ai_service.py: new "update_recurring" action with a target_name
  plus only the field(s) actually changing (amount/frequency/
  expectedDate/endDate, all optional) - a few-shot example
  distinguishes update phrasing ("change X to Y") from create
  phrasing, and the "recurring" action's own doc note now says to use
  it only for a plan that doesn't already exist.
- NaturalLanguageInput.jsx: new findMatchingPlan() looks up the
  target_name against the user's real recurringPlans - exact
  case-insensitive match first, then a substring match in either
  direction (the model may output a slightly longer/shorter name than
  what's stored, e.g. "...Subscription" vs not). A genuinely ambiguous
  multi-match is treated as no match rather than guessing which plan
  was meant, since silently updating the wrong one would be worse than
  the bug this fixes. On a match, calls the existing updateRecurringPlan
  action (merging only the changed fields into the existing plan,
  since the backend's PUT expects the full RecurringPlan shape). On no
  match, shows a clear error instead of silently creating a new plan -
  the exact behavior being fixed.

Verified: a standalone test of findMatchingPlan's exact/substring/
case-insensitive/no-match/ambiguous-match logic, and a full in-browser
run against the real app (mocking only the /ai/classify network call,
since I don't have live Gemini/Ollama credentials in this environment)
- created a "Google AI Pro" plan at 500, sent an update_recurring
action targeting "Google AI Pro Subscription" for 650, and confirmed
the existing plan updated in place (no duplicate) both on the
Dashboard's Month Projection and the Planner's commitment list.
Also confirmed a genuinely unmatched target_name shows the error
message and creates nothing.

Closes #58

decision: Refactor FinancialContext to manage household-related state and interactions separately.
rationale: Separating households management into its own context/module improves code organization, enhances readability by isolating functionality related specifically to handling multiple users (households) in a shared financial account. source_excerpt:
feat: household frontend - persona switcher, setup/join, member management

PR 3 of 3 for #45 (household/shared accounts). Builds on #51 and #52
(the backend model/invite flow and transaction/goal tagging) to wire
households into the actual UI.

- api.js: household CRUD/invite/join/member endpoints, plus a
  getScopeHeaders() helper (Authorization + X-Household-Id when a
  persona is active) applied only to the transaction and goal calls
  - the only two resources that are actually household-aware. The
  other ~25 existing call sites are untouched.
- FinancialContext: households list + activeHouseholdId (persisted
  to localStorage under the same key api.js reads, so a refresh
  keeps whichever persona was active), switchPersona() re-fetches
  just transactions/goals for the new persona, plus
  create/join/leave/delete household actions.
- Navigation.jsx: a persona switcher (avatar-stack-style trigger in
  the sidebar, a "Switch View" entry in the mobile More sheet) opens
  a panel listing Personal + each household, reusing the existing
  More-sheet backdrop/panel pattern rather than a new dropdown
  primitive.
- New HouseholdPage.jsx (route /household): inline create/join forms
  (matching BudgetsPage's pattern, not a multi-step wizard - the
  actual forms are one field each), plus per-household member
  management (invite generation, promote to owner, remove, leave,
  delete) for owners.
- JarVisualization.jsx: additive-only per-member contribution
  breakdown, shown only when goal.household_id is set. Personal
  goals are completely unaffected.

Verified end-to-end in-browser with two real accounts: created a
household as Alice, generated an invite, joined as Bob, added a
household-scoped transaction and goal deposit as Alice, confirmed
Bob sees the same shared transaction/goal with per-member
contributions correctly attributed (Alice +5000, Bob +2000 after his
own deposit), and confirmed switching either user back to "Personal"
shows a completely empty, isolated view with zero shared data
leaking through.

Ref #45

title: chore: making sure artifacts from package-lock.json remains unchanged
decision: Avoid modifying the contents of package-lock.json to ensure reproducible builds and consistent dependency management.
rationale: Changing artifacts from package-lock.json could lead to inconsistencies in dependencies across different environments, potentially causing unexpected behavior or conflicts. Sticking with unmodified lock files helps maintain stability and predictability in deployments.
alternatives: Updating the contents of package-lock.json manually after each change
Ignoring changes made by npm that affect package-lock.json

author: anubhab-m02
title: fix: validate Quick Add amounts against input text, fall back to Gemini on mismatch (#57)
decision: _amounts_plausible() method was implemented to validate Quick Add amounts against input text and fall back to Gemini on mismatch.
rationale: The rationale behind this decision is that the local model may silently round non-round amounts (e.g., 53200 -> 53000), which can lead to inaccuracies in amount validation. By implementing _amounts_plausible(), we ensure a more accurate and reliable comparison of Quick Add output with input text, thereby enhancing user experience by falling back on Gemini when discrepancies are detected.
alternatives: _extract_number_candidates() function was considered as an alternative but wasn't sufficient alone due to potential inaccuracies in amount validation.
source_excerpt: fix: validate Quick Add amounts against input text, fall back to Gemini on mismatch (#57)

author: anubhab-m02
title: fix: base achievements on distinct-day activity instead of point-in-time totals to prevent gaming
decision: Base achievements on distinct-day activity instead of point-in-time totals to prevent gaming.
rationale: This change aims to discourage users from unlocking rewards through a single lump-sum transaction or by creating multiple transactions in rapid succession, which could lead to exploitation. By requiring the total amount saved across several separate deposits and ensuring these are spread over distinct days, it ensures that achievements reflect consistent savings behavior rather than opportunistic gaming of point-in-time totals.
alternatives: Base achievements on raw transaction count
Require a single lump-sum transfer to unlock rewards
source_excerpt: fix: base achievements on distinct-day activity instead of point-in-time totals to prevent gaming

author: anubhab-m02
title: Request timeouts + ingestion orchestrator + POST /ingest
decision: Implemented configurable per-request timeouts and added ingestion orchestrator.
rationale: To improve fault tolerance by skipping malformed output, counting non-decisions/malformed outputs for each item/run (skip + count), being able to abort when encountering GitHub/Ollama errors without advancing the cursor. Also addressed missing test fixture in existing codebase through refactoring tests into a single autouse fixture.
alternatives: Skip implementing configurable per-request timeouts, leaving them unchanged as default values.
source_excerpt:
## Summary

- Closes #45
- Closes #22
- Closes #23

## Changelog

- Add configurable per-request timeouts (`github_request_timeout_seconds`, `ollama_request_timeout_seconds`) to every outbound GitHub/Ollama HTTP call, translating a GitHub timeout into `GitHubError` instead of hanging.
- Add the ingestion orchestrator (`ingestion/run.py`): `run_ingestion(repo)` ties `github_client` → `extract` → `embed` → `store` together, per-item fault-tolerant (skip + count non-decisions/malformed output) and per-run fail-loud (GitHub/Ollama errors abort without advancing the cursor).
- Add `POST /ingest` (`routers/ingest.py`), wired into `main.py`: runs a single repo when given, or every configured repo on an empty/absent body.
- Cleanup (found in ponytail review): moved the `REQUIRED_ENV`/`_settings_env` test fixture, copy-pasted across five test files, into one autouse fixture in `conftest.py`; dropped `sys.path.insert` boilerplate in two test files already covered by `conftest.py`; unified `_ingest_commits`/`_ingest_prs` in `run.py` into one generic `_ingest_items`. Also fixed a pre-existing bug this surfaced: `test_github_client.py`'s `fake_get` mocks didn't accept the `timeout` kwarg added earlier in this PR, silently breaking 5 `list_prs` tests until they were fixed here.

author: anubhab-m02
title: Retrieval: search with relevance floor + /retrieve and /repos endpoints
decision: Implement search functionality in retrieval module and add endpoints for retrieving data.
rationale: To improve search capabilities by embedding queries, configuring Chroma collection with cosine similarity scoring, filtering results based on relevance floor (0.3), adding a POST endpoint to retrieve specific items using 'RetrieveRequest', and providing an endpoint that lists all configured repositories along with their indexed-unit count while still showing repos without any units.
alternatives: Continue searching for alternative libraries or frameworks instead of Chroma collection
Skip the relevance floor filter as it may reduce performance
source_excerpt:
## Summary

- Closes #24
- Closes #25
- Closes #26

## Changelog

- Add `retrieval/search.py`: `search(query, k, repos)` embeds the query via `embed.embed_text`, retrieves top-k via a new `store.query_units` (Chroma collection now configured for cosine similarity, score = 1 - distance), and drops results below `RELEVANCE_FLOOR` (0.3).
- Add `POST /retrieve` (`routers/retrieve.py`), wired into `main.py`: thin wiring from `RetrieveRequest` to `search()` and back to `RetrieveResponse`.
- Add `GET /repos` (`routers/repos.py`), wired into `main.py`: lists each configured repo with its indexed-unit count via a new `store.count_units(repo)` helper (Chroma metadata `where` filter); repos with zero indexed units still appear.
- Cleanup (found in ponytail review): the `make_unit()` DecisionUnit-factory helper had been copy-pasted into three test files (including `test_store.py`, left over from before the conftest consolidation two PRs ago). Centralized into one `make_unit` fixture in `conftest.py`, following the same pattern as the existing `load_fixture` fixture. Also dropped a `REQUIRED_ENV`/manual-env-loop reintroduced in `test_search.py` that duplicated conftest's autouse fixture — matched it to `test_repos_router.py`'s existing minimal-override pattern instead.
